How to plan a website redesign without losing useful pages

Audit content and URLs before changing the visual system.

NITESH PATEL · WEB DEVELOPMENT NOTES · 2026

Audit content and URLs before changing the visual system. This guide looks at the decisions that matter before and after the page goes live.

Start with the real need

Begin with a page inventory. Record which URLs exist, what each page is for and which pages bring visitors or enquiries. A redesign can accidentally remove the very content people use.

Plan the structure

Interview the people who maintain the site and those who answer enquiries. Their recurring questions reveal where the current structure is confusing.

Make practical choices

Prototype the most important route first, then apply the visual system to the other pages. Preserve or redirect URLs deliberately when their content changes.

Check the result

After launch, verify navigation, forms, redirects, metadata and analytics. Monitor actual search and enquiry data for issues the design review did not reveal.

Apply this to your own site

Start with the page your visitors use most. Review its purpose, the questions it answers and the action it supports. Then make one measurable improvement at a time.
